step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram shows an incoming request routed through an edge/routing tier (Route 53, CloudFront, internal Route 53) to split traffic between two backend compute paths (ECS on Fargate vs. API Gateway with Lambda). CloudWatch monitors performance and triggers a Lambda function (labeled AWS SDK) that updates routing weights back in the internal Route 53. Both compute tiers interact with a suite of databases: ElastiCache, DocumentDB, RDS, and OpenSearch (labeled ElasticSearch). AWS CDK is drawn as an infrastructure-as-code deployment block without direct runtime data flow lines.

graph.name: Zigbang Hybrid Architecture with Duplexing Method
graph.notes: The architecture uses dynamic DNS weight adjustment via Route 53, CloudWatch, and Lambda (AWS SDK) to balance high traffic across ECS Fargate and API Gateway Lambda backends.

edges.notes: Public Route 53 resolves traffic to CloudFront
CloudFront forwards requests to internal Route 53
Internal Route 53 routes weighted traffic to ECS
Internal Route 53 routes weighted traffic to API Gateway
ECS metrics are sent to CloudWatch
CloudWatch triggers Lambda (AWS SDK) on alarm or metric update
Lambda (AWS SDK) dynamically updates internal Route 53 record weights
